| atr | Volatility → stops/sizing | Converts the tape into position math |

**Deliberately excluded to avoid redundancy:** `macds` (its only use is the cross vs. MACD, which `macdh` expresses more directly), `boll`/`boll_ub` (the middle band is a 20 SMA duplicating the 50 SMA family; the upper band at 242.25 is ~12% above spot and irrelevant to a sub-222 regime), and `vwma` (the moving-average family is already crowded at three timeframes — I read raw daily volume from the OHLCV CSV instead, which is more informative here than a fourth average).

## 3) Multi-timeframe structure: three clocks disagreeing

**Long-term — intact and rising.** The 200 SMA climbed from 195.59 (2026-08-31) to 203.84 (2026-10-28), +4.22% in under two months, and spot at 215.38 sits **+5.66% above it**. The 50 SMA is 18.16 points *above* the 200 SMA (8.91% spread) — a bullish alignment that puts a death cross weeks away at any plausible price path. This is a correction inside an uptrend, not a trend change.

**Medium-term — turning over for the first time.** The 50 SMA peaked at 223.09 on 2026-10-14 and has printed lower values six sessions straight (222.96 → 222.00). It is still *rising* versus August (208.39 on 2026-08-31), but the slope has broken. Price closed below the 50 SMA every session since 2026-10-14, and at 215.38 trades **-2.98% under it**. The 50 SMA and the Bollinger middle band (223.79) now overlap into a dense ~222–224 resistance shelf.

**Short-term — down but decelerating.** The 10 EMA fell from 232.61 (2026-10-07) to 217.51, and price is 2.13 points (0.98%) below it. However the *rate* of decay is flattening: roughly -1.18/session (10-07→10-16), -0.85/session (10-16→10-28), and only **-0.31/session over the last three sessions** (218.44 → 217.51). A flattening fast MA after a 6.5% decline is the fingerprint of a base attempting to form — but a base is not a breakout.

**The drawdown, measured.** Highest close in the window: 239.24 (2026-10-06); intraday high 243.37 the same day. To 215.38 today = **-9.97% on closes**; to the 210.18 intraday low of 2026-10-23 = **-13.6% peak-to-trough**. From that 210.96 close the stock rallied +3.31% to 217.94 by 2026-10-27 and then gave back -1.17% today.

**One-year context that changes the framing.** NVDA closed at 206.55 on 2025-10-29 and 215.38 today — **+4.27% in twelve months**, with a 12-month close range of 164.79 (2026-03-30) to 239.24 (2026-10-06), a 45%-wide box. Today's price sits at ~68% of that range. Over 18 months (from 109.87 on 2025-04-01) it is +96.0%. **So the honest read is: a strong long-term uptrend that has spent the last year oscillating rather than trending.** That argues for trading levels, not narratives.

## 4) Momentum: negative state, improving acceleration, no reversal yet

- **MACD state:** line -2.66 < signal -1.53, both below zero (line crossed under zero 2026-10-16). Downward momentum is the *established* regime.
- **MACD histogram:** -2.39 (2026-10-19) → -2.16 (10-23) → -1.79 (10-26) → -1.33 (10-27) → **-1.13 (10-28)** — three consecutive improving prints, i.e. the second derivative has turned up while the first is still negative.
- **Two mild, and I stress mild, positive divergences:** on 2026-10-16 price closed 214.13 with histogram -2.3656; on 2026-10-23 price closed *lower* at 210.96 with a *less negative* histogram of -2.1589. Same pair on RSI: 37.56 → 38.11 on a lower close. Magnitudes are tiny (0.21 and 0.55 points) — this is a *hint*, not a signal.
- **RSI 43.88:** up from the 38.11 trough (10-23) but down from 46.31 yesterday, and nowhere near 30. Note what this means: RSI never reached oversold at 210.96, and never topped 67.27 (2026-10-06) during the run. Momentum has been rangebound between ~37 and ~67 all quarter — **the classic signature of a market where "overbought/oversold" thresholds don't fire and RSI must be traded as a middle-band oscillator.**
- **The counter-evidence nobody should ignore:** the histogram improved today on a *down* day while the MACD line actually deteriorated marginally (-2.58 → -2.66). This is exactly the pattern that precedes a failed bounce in a low-conviction tape.

## 5) Volatility and the Bollinger geometry — the single most useful number here

ATR is 5.91 = **2.74% of spot**. It has compressed from 7.47 (2026-08-31) and 7.07 (2026-09-10), ticked up to 6.24 (10-22) during the leg down, and is now easing (6.11 → 5.94 → 5.91).

%B position: (215.38 − 205.32) / (242.25 − 205.32) = **0.27** — the lower quartile of the bands, below the middle band since 2026-10-08, but **never closed at or below the lower band** during the entire decline. The lower band itself fell fast (217.82 on 10-14 → 208.06 on 10-23, with the steepest -2.10 single-step on 10-22→10-23) and the decline has slowed to ~-0.91/session since. Falling lower band = sellers still control direction; *decelerating* fall = they're running out of ammo.

**The critical volatility insight for stop placement:** the 2026-10-22→10-23 low (210.18) to the 10-28 high (219.99) is only **~1.7× ATR wide**. The entire current "battle" fits inside one volatility unit. That is *why* the 10-21 push to 221.97/222.19 collapsed and why 10-26/10-27's recovery stalled at 219.99 — nothing has yet broken a distance that exceeds noise. **Any stop set tighter than ~1.5× ATR (≈8.9 points) from a 215 entry is a noise-stop, not a risk-stop.**

## 6) Volume & candle structure — the bounce is unconvincing

10-session average volume ≈ **98.7M**. Distribution days were heavy: 127.1M (10-15), 121.3M (10-16), 125.4M on the -4.4% day of **10-22** (219.88-open structure, close 212.21). The recovery days were *light*: 90.8M (10-26), 84.8M (10-27), and **91.7M today — ~7% below the 10-day mean**. Rising price on shrinking volume into a falling 50 SMA is a low-quality bounce.

Today's candle is the tell: **opened 219.88 above yesterday's 217.94 close, rallied to 219.99, and closed 215.38 — in the bottom 16% of the day's range** (214.47 low), below the 10 EMA. It printed a marginally higher intraday high (219.99 vs 219.19) on a lower close. Rejection right at the 10 EMA / 220 psychological line, not at the 50 SMA — the bears didn't even have to defend 222.

Episodic-gap risk is empirically high in this tape: **+8.74%** on 2026-08-27 (209.43→227.73) on 298.9M shares vs 179.9M prior; **-5.45%** (195.10→184.46) then **-4.16%** (→176.78) on 2026-02-26/27 on 360.8M and 311.6M shares; **-6.20%** on 2026-06-05. The dataset doesn't label catalysts, but the pattern is unambiguous: NVDA reprices violently and in clusters. Gapped stops will not fill where you expect — size accordingly.

## 7) Actionable framework — four playbooks, each with its own trigger

| Playbook | Trigger (must be on a *close*) | Entry zone | Stop | Target | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A. Trend resumption (long) | Close > 222.00 (50 SMA) with volume > ~110M | 222.5–224 | 214.47 (10-28 low, ≈1.3× ATR) | 227.2 / 230.9, then 239.24 | Only a close through 222–223.79 invalidates the "lower high" sequence |
| B. Mean-reversion long | Tag of 205–207 (boll_lb 205.32) + RSI < 35 + histogram < -2.4 then improving | 205–207 | Below 202.5 (≈1.5× ATR; 200 SMA at 203.84 is the invalidation line) | 215 → 222 | Trades the box's lower edge into a *rising* long-term floor; best R:R in the set |
| C. Short / hedge into strength | Rejection between 218 and 222, close back below 10 EMA 217.51 | 216–218 (today already qualifies) | 224.5 (above the 50 SMA + 0.5× ATR) | 210.18, then 205.32 | Fades a falling fast MA into overlapping 50 SMA / Bollinger mid |
| D. No position | Price stays inside 210.18–219.99 | — | — | — | The range is <1.7× ATR: it is noise, not information. Stand aside |

**Preferred current stance for an unlevered swing account: neutral, mildly defensive.** Rationale: the long-term trend is up (above a rising 200 SMA), so outright bearishness is wrong here; but price is below both the 10 EMA and a *rolling-over* 50 SMA, MACD is negative, the bounce is on below-average volume, and today's close came in the low of the range. That combination says **"don't chase at 215, don't panic-shore above 205 — wait for the box to resolve."** A 215 entry with a structurally sound (1.5× ATR) stop risks ~9–10 points to reach 205 while the nearest clean reward zone is 219–222; **the risk/reward from mid-range is the worst available in this structure.** If forced to act today: trim gross exposure into the 218–222 shelf rather than initiate new longs.

**Escalate conviction downward if:** closes lose 210.18 (10-23 low) → the 210–222 box has failed on the downside, and the 200 SMA / Bollinger-lower confluence at 203.8–205.3 becomes a magnet; a close below 203.84 would flip the long-term trend argument itself.
**Escalate conviction upward only if:** a close above 222.00 with above-average volume, ideally with MACD histogram crossing positive — that sequence would take the price above both the 50 SMA and the middle band and flip the medium-term clock that is currently pointing down.
**Watch the 50 SMA print:** if it keeps declining from 222.00 while price stays at 212–218, resistance is compressing downward and the "base" is likely a shelf, not a floor.

## 8) Limitations

Historical swings cited above are all directly traceable to dated closes/highs/lows in the returned data; I have **not** asserted any named catalyst (earnings, guidance, macro) for the 2026-08-27, 2026-02-26/27 or 2026-06-05 moves, because no tool output labels them. The MACD/RSI divergences are quantitatively small (0.21 and 0.55 points) and unconfirmed by a bullish MACD/signal cross. Bollinger middle/upper bands and MACD signal line are quoted from the verified snapshot only (not independently re-fetched per-day), so day-by-day band-width change is inferred from the lower band alone.

## The core bull claim: NVDA’s growth is not slowing — it is still compounding at an absurd scale

The most recent filed quarter, three months ended **2026-07-26**, is the anchor:

- Revenue: **$96.22B**, up **17.9% sequentially** and **105.9% year over year**.

**$57.0B → $68.1B implied → $81.6B → $96.2B**

That is roughly **18–20% sequential growth per step**, with no visible crack in the latest quarter. For the bull case, this matters: NVDA is not relying on a one-time “AI hype” quarter. It is repeatedly lapping enormous comparisons while expanding profit dollars faster than revenue. H1 FY2027 revenue was up **95.8%** year over year, while net income was up **161.1%** — that is operating leverage in action. The bear’s cheapest shot is “competition” or “ASIC substitution.” But the fundamentals and market chatter still point to NVDA as the default premium AI platform:

- NVDA’s **$3B reported investment into Meta’s share offering**, if confirmed, reinforces ecosystem linkage between the largest AI compute supplier and a hyperscaler/customer with capital appetite.

AMD is a real competitor. ASICs are a real risk. But “AMD catching up” and “NVIDIA still has 75% gross margins with 106% YoY revenue growth” are very different things.
